items.title: Player interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2012
items.q: "it’s like Gerald was speaking about call and response in the music yesterday."

ctx.x: Yesterday you played in Utica. And I was wondering, because both you and your drummer were talking about how joyful and active this New Orleans music is. And is it different to perform for an audience that maybe isn’t as engaged as an audience in New Orleans might be?

Yeah. I think it’s always good for us if the audience is engaged. You know we feed off of that energy. In New Orleans that’s very common when you’re performing or if it’s a parade, or whatever it is, when — it’s like Gerald was speaking about call and response in the music yesterday. When something is done, somebody else takes up where that’s left off. And it’s always a conversation. If it’s the music, or if you ever watched a second line dancers dancing, you know if you see one person doing one dance, then…
Yeah. I think you talked about having — that New Orleans music can mean something different to everybody. You had to make your own connection to it somehow.
